text.title: Go HTTP Handlers (Gin / Echo / Chi / stdlib) Output Contract
text.summary: Pins the shape of a valid Go HTTP Handlers (Gin / Echo / Chi / stdlib) output. Subagent MUST satisfy this contract before returning to caller.

required.field: the actual answer / chosen option / value produced
at least 2 sentences; cites at least one input artefact by name
list of input names with source paths or URLs

forbidden.pattern: rationale that does not reference any input by name
inputs_used empty AND decision is not 'no-op'
duplicate artefact_id within the same store

allowed-transformations.transformation: Trim rationale to no more than 500 chars, preserving numeric claims and named tools.
Promote 'no decision yet' to status='pending' rather than fabricating a decision.
Group near-duplicate inputs, recording the group with member count.

section.title: Server-shape contract (what the artefact describes)
section.p: The artefact above records the DECISION. This section pins the server and handler shape that decision must produce — framework, middleware order, all four timeouts, drain window, and the handler thinness bound.

example.note: gin.New + explicit middleware + four timeouts + a thin handler on the request context.

list.item: Every required field populated with a typed value
No forbidden pattern matches the output
Middleware order: Recovery, RequestID, Logger, ErrorMapper, Auth, then domain
http.Server sets all four timeouts explicitly (no zero values)
Every handler is under 40 lines and carries no business logic
c.Request.Context() plumbed to every service / repo call; no context.Background()
No `go func() { ... c.Request... }` inside a handler
Validation lives in request-struct binding tags, not the handler body
main() registers SIGINT/SIGTERM and calls srv.Shutdown(ctx) with a 10-15s drain
